title: Authoring Guide
subtitle: How to write and publish a manual in this repository
description: Every content block and inline syntax the builder supports, with live examples. Internal: kept off the live site.

sections.title: Workflow
sections.summary: One JSON file per manual. The builder checks it, then renders the site and the PDF from it.

blocks.alt: JSON manuals go into build.py, which writes the HTML site and the PDF.
blocks.caption: From JSON to site and PDF.

items: Scaffold a manual: `python builder/build.py --new methodology "Methodology"`. It starts as a draft with `"publish": false`.
Write its sections in `content/manuals/methodology.json`. Your editor checks the file against `schema/manual.schema.json` as you type, through its `$schema` line.
Run `build.cmd`. It validates every manual, builds `site/` including drafts, prints the PDFs and opens the site.
When the manual is ready, set `"publish": true` and push. GitHub Actions rebuilds the live site and its PDFs.

blocks.text: The build stops on any problem: a schema error, an unknown glossary term, a broken cross-reference, a missing figure file, or a published manual linking to an unpublished one. It lists every problem with its location.

A manual has metadata, `sections`, optional `appendices` (lettered A, B, …) and an optional `changelog`. Sections nest to any depth through their own `sections` array and are numbered automatically, so reordering never means renumbering. A section `id` is its permanent anchor: links use it, so keep it stable when titles change.

blocks.caption: Manual metadata fields.
rows: Equals the file name; used in URLs and cross-references.
Shown on the page, the cover and the landing card.
`status` is `draft`, `review` or `final`. Drafts get a banner online and on the PDF cover.
`PLEXOS`, `PyPSA` or both. Shown as badges. Sections and entries take it too.
`false` keeps the manual off the live site.
Landing-page position; how many heading levels the contents list shows.

blocks.text: A section can also carry `summary` (a lead paragraph) and `sources`, the workspace files it was written from. Sources print under the section, so a reader can see where a statement comes from.

blocks.caption: Inline markup inside any text field.
rows: [[snsp]] links to the glossary, with the definition on hover.

blocks.title: Backslashes and dollars
text: JSON needs every backslash doubled, so TeX's `\frac` is written `\\frac` in the file.
Inline maths uses GitLab's `` $`…`$ `` form, so a plain `$` (as in $/kW) is never taken for maths.

sections.title: Content blocks
sections.summary: Each entry in a section's `blocks` has a `type`. Any block may have an `id`; tables, figures, diagrams and equations are then numbered and can be cited.

blocks.text: `text` takes one string or an array of paragraphs. `list` takes strings or `{"text", "items"}` objects for nesting:
`entries` renders record cards, one per item, with the fields named in the block. This is the form for inputs, parameters and result variables:

items.title: Node hourly load
items.method: Each province's shape is scaled to its share of national demand; a node is the sum of its provinces.

blocks.text: `equation` takes KaTeX in `tex` and an optional `where` legend:
Cite it as [@#eq-energy]. `callout` has five kinds:
`diagram` draws Mermaid source; `figure` shows an image from `content/assets/`, such as [@#fig-pipeline]:

blocks.caption: Demand chain, as a Mermaid diagram.

text: Terms live once, in `content/glossary.json`, and every manual shares them. Reference a term as `[[id]]`. Online the term links to the glossary page, which lists the manuals that use it. Each PDF gets a *Terms used* appendix with only its own terms, so it stands on its own.
Add a term before you use it; an unknown id stops the build.

items: Create an empty GitHub repository and add it as this repo's `origin`.
In the repository's Settings → Pages, set Source to *GitHub Actions*.
Put the site address in `content/site.json` `base_url`, so links between manuals inside a PDF point to the live site.
Push to `main`. The workflow in `.github/workflows/pages.yml` validates, builds the site and the PDFs, and deploys them.
